title: personal-okr-weekly-checkin-harper-wong-2026-03-21
content:
WIP personal OKR check-in (week ending 2026-03-21) - notes to self

OBJECTIVE 1: Reduce p95 tail latency for short-text generation (<= 300 tokens)
- KR1.1: p95 latency <= 120ms on ga4-small across 95% of traffic buckets (baseline 180ms)
- KR1.2: Reduce variance (stdev) of request latency by 20% from baseline
- KR1.3: Ship continuous-batching improvements to prod for short requests (canary -> 100%)

Weekly update:
- Measurements: p95 currently ~145ms on ga4-small across staged canary (improved from 160ms last week). Still above target but moving in right direction.
- Rolled out small change to batch scheduling (PR 987) to prioritize short requests; saw 8% p95 improvement in canary traffic.
- Added extra metric tags to trace short vs long request paths; found ~4% of requests hitting slower kernel due to sequence length misclassification (edgecases).
- Variance: stdev down ~10% in canary, still need another 10% to hit KR.

Blocking issues / risks:
- One regression in mem-util for a subset of requests when batch size > 8 (investigating memory spike). Potential rollback if not resolved by EOD Fri.
- Need infra time to run a full load test with mixed traffic; SRE queue is long. Follow-up with Jenna (SRE) and link to JIRA-1842.

Next week plan:
- Finish investigation for mem-util regression; add guardrail to cap batch size per-queue until root cause fixed.
- Expand canary to 20% traffic if mem spike is mitigated; monitor p95 and error rate closely.
- Work with product to collect prioritized short-request customer flows to ensure representative workload.
- Start experiments for KV cache warmup to further reduce variance (quick prototype + A/B).

Actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Add automated check to CI to detect kernel misclassification (ticket: JIRA-1857)
- [ ] Schedule SRE load window (blocked -> ping Jenna)
- [ ] Draft ops runbook for batch-size guardrail and rollback steps
- [ ] Pair with Maya on telemetry dashboard updates for per-route p95 breakdown

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could try adaptive batch sizing: prefer smaller batches for queues that historically have short sequences. Might need per-customer profile.
- Investigate quantization variant impact on short-request p95 (maybe faster kernel exists).
- Keep an eye on cost impact of more aggressive caching; speak with finance if hit looks like +10%.

Questions for 1:1 with manager (Avery):
- Prioritize time: how much SRE support is reasonable vs pushing a mitigatory software fix?
- Thresholds: confirm tolerance for memory spike if p95 benefit is >20% (is tradeoff acceptable?)

Quick retrospective on last sprint:
- What went well: smaller PRs helped get faster reviews (thanks Maya). Canary showed measurable p95 win quickly.
- What could be better: earlier load test plan would have caught mem issue sooner. Need to build load testing into PR checklist for serving runtime changes.

END -- rough draft. Will tidy before publishing to people ops/manager.
